scenario: Brightwick Mills is a small invented studio that sells a photo-sharing app called Lumenfold. Last week a launch campaign tripled the number of uploads in two hours. The upload queue grew until some photos took ten minutes to appear. The team has one afternoon to decide what to change before the next campaign.
constraints: Assume 400 uploads per second at the peak and 90 per second on a normal day.
Assume each photo is 3 MB and must be visible to followers within 30 seconds.
The team has two engineers and no budget for a new vendor this quarter.
deliverable: A one-page decision note that names the bottleneck, the change, and how the team will know it worked.

reference_answer.title: Restate the problem
reference_answer.body: Uploads outran the workers that resize photos, so the queue grew. The goal is a 30 second visibility target at 400 uploads per second.

reference_answer.title: Find the bottleneck
reference_answer.body: At 400 per second and 3 MB each the intake moves 1.2 GB per second. The resize workers, not the storage, were saturated first.

reference_answer.title: Choose the change
reference_answer.body: Scale the resize workers with the queue depth, and show the original photo at once while the resized copy is made.

reference_answer.title: Name the trade-off
reference_answer.body: Showing the original first costs bandwidth for followers on slow links. It buys the 30 second target without new vendors.

reference_answer.title: Define the check
reference_answer.body: Alert when the oldest queued photo is older than 20 seconds. Replay the campaign load in a test before the next launch.

rubric: States the visibility target and the peak rate as numbers.
Names the resize workers as the bottleneck and says why.
Proposes one change that fits two engineers and no new vendor.
Names one trade-off of the change.
Defines a measurable check, such as the age of the oldest queued photo.
The answer fits on one page and leads with the decision.
common_mistakes: Adding servers everywhere without finding the bottleneck first.
Giving no number for the target, so nobody can tell whether the fix worked.
Proposing a new vendor when the brief rules one out.
